newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania radio reports cholera among Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania radio reports cholera among Zaire refugees.

text.p: One man has died and 16 people have been taken to hospital in an outbreak of cholera among Zairean and Rwandan refugees in western Tanzania, state-run Radio Tanzania said on Thursday.
The Swahili-language bulletin said the outbreak occurred in western Kigoma, where about 50,000 refugees have arrived since November 1 fleeing fighting in eastern Zaire.

Radio Tanzania quoted the regional medical officer as saying a total of 23 cholera cases had been detected so far among the mostly Zairean refugees staying at three temporary sites in and around Kigoma town.
He called for measures to prevent the disease from spreading among the local population.

The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR is known to be concerned about overcrowded conditions in the three holding centres and has advertised for local transport operators to help move the refugees to permanent camps outside Kigoma.
One of the biggest problems preventing a quick and orderly evacuation of the temporary sites has been an acute lack of transport, UNHCR head of mission in Kigoma, John Adu, told Reuters last week.

The refugees are living in overcrowded conditions in a football stadium, a government compound and a warehouse at the port. Kigoma, a strategic railhead town, is Tanzania's only port on Lake Tanganyika.
